blocks.text: The two pointers do not create nested work: `read` contributes exactly n visits and `write` contributes at most n increments inside those visits, so n + at-most-n primitive updates is O(n). O(1) and O(log n) time cannot cover reading all n input positions; O(n log n) and O(n^2) are not tight because there is no sorting or nested pair scan. Accepted values are written back into the existing array and only a fixed number of indices or counters are stored, so auxiliary space is O(1), not O(log n) or O(n). The input array and its returned logical prefix are reused storage, not an additional allocation.
